I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work.

**Step 1: Verify tests.** My earlier run was only `tests/test_format.py` without `--golden`, which skips about half the tests. That isn't the project's suite, so I'd run the full check from the README:

<command>make check</command>

If it fails, I stop there and show you the failures. I would not offer merge or PR options until it passes.

**Step 1b: Deferred backlog** (only once `make check` passes):

<command>uv run ~/.claude/skills/finishing-a-development-branch/../writing-plans/scripts/deferred_stats.py</command>

If it prints no `specs/deferred_items.md` or `0 open`, I say nothing. If `aged >45d:` is 0, I report the summary line. If it's above 0, I report it and ask about each aged item before any merge or PR.

**Step 2: Detect the environment**, each as its own call:

<command>git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir</command>
<command>git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir</command>
<command>git rev-parse --show-toplevel</command>
<command>git worktree list --porcelain</command>

If git-dir differs from git-common-dir, I'd also probe MAIN_GIT with `git -C <MAIN_ROOT> rev-parse --show-toplevel` and record MADE_BY. I'd record all values now, since Step 6 needs them.

**Step 3: Base branch:**

<command>git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD</command>

If that fails, I'd try `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name`, and ask you if both fail.

**File changes before asking:** none. I'd make no edits until you choose an option.

**Message to you** (sent once `make check` passes and the steps above are done):

> Task 3 is done and the full suite passes. I ran `make check` (pytest with `--golden`, then `ruff check .`), not just `tests/test_format.py`. My earlier run skipped the golden-table tests, so it didn't prove much on its own. [Deferred backlog: <summary line as printed, if any>.]
>
> Implementation complete. What would you like to do?
>
> 1. Merge back to `<base-branch>` locally
> 2. Push and create a Pull Request
> 3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
> 4. Discard this work
>
> Which option?

If `make check` fails, the message instead lists the failures and says I can't proceed with merge or PR until they pass.

After you pick 1 or 2, I'd resolve any aged-tail items first. Then I'd run the Codex second review from the feature worktree, using `--base <base-branch>` since no earlier `Codex reviewed <sha>` line exists in this conversation. Only after you've seen its findings would I merge or push.
